newsitem.title: USA: Georgia counties plan sales tax votes for schools.
newsitem.headline: Georgia counties plan sales tax votes for schools.

text.p: Several Georgia counties have scheduled March referendums on a newly authorized local-option sales tax to fund school contruction, according to newspaper reports and school district officials Friday.

In November, voters approved a state constitutional amendment allowing school districts to seek one-cent sale tax hikes to build new schools or retire outstanding construction debt. Previously, only property taxes could be used for school contruction.

School boards in Fulton, Gwinnett, Clarke and Meriwether counties voted Thursday night to put the tax before voters in March 18 referendums. The tax requires a local district voter approval and can be levied for five years.
The tax would raise about $500 million in Fulton County, $550 million in Gwinnett County, $90 million in Clarke County and $7 million in Meriwether County.
Douglas and Paulding counties had previously approved March 18 referendums.
Four other districts -- City of Atlanta and Clayton, DeKalb and Columbia counties willl decide next week whether to call March 18 referendums on the tax hike in their districts.
Since U.S. Justice Department rules require 60 days notice for such referendums, Georgia school boards must decide by Jan. 16 whether to hold March 18 referendums. Four
counties -- Cobb, Henry, Marietta and Cherokee -- have already said they will considering September referendums.
